role: Fire Protection System Designer (Sprinkler/Suppression Design Engineer)

evidence.quote: My job was to take the existing system, which was designed for a much lighter occupancy, and redesign it to handle the new storage configuration, get it through plan review, and get it installed before the tenant's lease start.
evidence.explanation: Redesigning an existing infrastructure-constrained system to satisfy new hazard/storage requirements within a fixed schedule requires generating and sequencing a non-routine solution, not merely applying a fixed rule.

evidence.quote: I pulled the NFPA design density and area curves for that classification at 32 feet of rack height, picked a density/area point that cleared the code minimum, and built out the hydraulic calculations.
evidence.explanation: Selecting and assembling a design basis from multiple code-permitted alternatives to fit a specific building and rack configuration is a design/problem-resolution act, combining technical constraints into a coherent solution.

evidence.quote: the in-rack sprinkler allowance was the biggest line item I could trim ... so I recommended pulling the in-rack allowance to hit his number.
evidence.explanation: Devising a cost-reduction approach that reconciles budget constraints with protection requirements is an adaptive design/resolution task.
